newsitem.title: BOSNIA: British base hit in latest Bosnian attack.
newsitem.headline: British base hit in latest Bosnian attack.

text.p: Several explosive devices were hurled at a British base in Bosnia overnight, in the fourth apparent retaliation for last week's NATO raid on two Serbs indicted for war crimes.
The devices -- possibly hand grenades -- were lobbed into the base car park in the Bosnian Serb-controlled town of Banja Luka, Western officials said on Thursday.
British peacekeeping soldiers fired warning shots and detained four suspects after the incident, a NATO officer said.
"At 22:45 there were two small explosions at the wood factory (British base) in Banja Luka followed by a third explosion," the officer, who asked not to be named, said.
"The intruders were challenged and two were apprehended 20 minutes later and two a short time after that," the officer added.
A fourth explosion and a burst of gunfire was heard several hours later a short distance from the base.
No one was seriously injured in the incident, which was being invesitgated by British military police and local Serb police. The suspects were turned over the Serb authorities.
Initial reports indicated the explosives were not meant to cause injuries, the officer said.
The incident marked the fourth small-scale explosives attack in four days in apparent retaliation for a NATO raid last week on two Serbs indicted for war crimes.
Previous bombings targeted international monitors working in Bosnia's Serb republic for the United Nations or the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.

The NATO-led peace force has received anonymous threats since British special forces arrested one war crimes suspect and shot dead another who resisted arrest last Thursday in Prijedor, near Banja Luka.
Both suspects were wanted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Netherlands for allegedly orchestrating a brutal "ethnic cleansing" campaign against Moslems and Croats in the Prijedor region.

A U.S. soldier suffered minor injuries on Wednesday when a man cut him with a hand-sickle in northeast Bosnia. The incident was still under investigation and NATO said it was unclear if that attack was connected to the bombings.
